conclusion: The guard test_no_two_docs_share_a_number detects duplicate leading numbers (05-a.md and 05-b.md) but does not detect a document renamed without its number changing when citations use bare references (such as docs/08). An exhaustive census confirms zero tests across the repository read document body content, validate H1 headings against filenames, or verify citation semantic validity.
confidence: High across all measurements. The findings are verified by the 20-mutant battery in hunts/r_c62e44/probe.py executed against a clean sandbox under baseline and per-mutant undo controls, along with a complete static census of all 37 test files mentioning docs/.

threads.what: Document filename slugs and H1 titles are unconstrained against each other, allowing complete drift between title and filename.
threads.why_it_might_matter: Contributors and agents navigating by number and slug can see contradictory subject descriptions without tripping any CI check.
threads.first_step: Add an assertion in tests/test_docs_numbering.py verifying that words from the filename slug appear in the document H1 heading.

threads.what: Subdirectories of docs/ are unscanned by tests/test_docs_numbering.py because _numbered_docs() uses non-recursive os.listdir.
threads.why_it_might_matter: Numbered documents accidentally placed under subdirectories like docs/doors/ or docs/reviews/ would bypass collision and gap checks.
threads.first_step: Add a check in tests/test_docs_numbering.py verifying that no numbered markdown files exist in subdirectories of docs/.

threads.what: The filename slug regex allows trailing dots and symbols (^(\d{2})-[\w.-]+\.md$).
threads.why_it_might_matter: Allows malformed filenames like 08-foo..md to match as numbered documents.
threads.first_step: Tighten the regex in tests/test_docs_numbering.py to ^(\d{2})-[a-z0-9-]+\.md$.
